rules.statement: In a test, make concurrent runs overlap with an explicit gate, where each side writes a ready marker and waits with a deadline for the other's, and assert that they did overlap, instead of relying on a fixed sleep.
rules.why: A fixed sleep doesn't guarantee overlap on a loaded machine, so the test can pass without proving what it claims, and it adds time to every run.
rules.check: Look for Start-Sleep, Thread.Sleep or Task.Delay used to make concurrent work overlap in tests, with no handshake and no assertion that the overlap happened.

rules.statement: When a change adds a best-effort or failure-handling branch, such as a cleanup that may fail without failing the run, add a test that forces that branch to run and asserts what it outputs.
rules.why: If a branch is never run by any test, a broken message or a failure that turns a pass into an error goes unnoticed.
rules.check: Check that new error, fallback or cleanup-failure paths in the diff have a test that triggers them, for example by holding a file open or removing write permission.

rules.statement: A best-effort delete that ignores errors must check afterwards whether the target still exists and report its path if it does, not fail silently.
rules.why: If a locked file stops the delete, the folder stays behind and nobody is told.
rules.check: Look for Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue, or a delete in a swallowed try/catch, with no later existence check and message.

rules.statement: When several scripts or classes need the same cleanup logic and its message, move it into one shared helper that they all call, instead of copying it into each one.
rules.why: Copies have to be changed one by one and drift apart over time.
rules.check: Look for the same multi-line cleanup or lifecycle block pasted into many files in a diff.

rules.statement: A line kept only for a non-obvious side effect, such as reading a process handle so that ExitCode stays available after the process exits, gets a comment that says why.
rules.why: Without the comment, a later author may delete the line or copy it without knowing what it guards against.
rules.check: Look for discarded reads or assignments, such as `$null = $x.Handle`, that have no comment explaining them.

rules.statement: When a run's behavior has an exception to its stated rule, such as deleting its empty work folder when there's nothing to run, the help text or docs must state that exception.
rules.why: Help text that doesn't match the behavior misleads users.
rules.check: Compare the help or doc comments with the branches in the diff that differ from the documented rule.

rules.statement: Don't raise a finding again on a pull request after the maintainer declined it in an earlier round, unless the code it concerns has changed since that reply.
rules.why: The maintainer declined repeats as already answered, with links to the earlier replies.
rules.check: Before reporting, look through earlier review rounds on the PR for the same concern and the maintainer's decline.

rules.statement: Don't ask for a behavioral test that runs a fixture copied from the real code when the shared pieces that code calls are already tested by behavior and a structural check pins each copy's use of them.
rules.why: A fixture built like the real code tests only the fixture's copy, not the real code, so it adds cost without adding coverage.
rules.check: Before asking for a fixture test, check whether the helper and the end-to-end path are already tested directly, and whether a text or structure check already covers each real caller.

rules.statement: Don't ask for new tests of behavior that a pull request leaves unchanged from the main branch; limit test requests to what the diff changes.
rules.why: The maintainer added a test only for the changed default and left the unchanged delete in an existing finally block untested in that PR.
rules.check: Before asking for a test, check in the diff whether the behavior is new or changed, or whether it predates the PR.

rules.statement: Don't report a test that's skipped only in an unusual local environment, such as running as root, when CI runs and passes that check.
rules.why: The check is still covered where it matters, and the skip affects only local runs.
rules.check: Before reporting a skip, check whether the CI runner meets the skip condition and whether the CI logs show the check passing.
